A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGD research, retaining Algorithm 1, the training objective, and core experimental results. All 32 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and diagnostic analyses, including Tables 1–2 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds HumanEval, Qwen2.5-Math, AIME sampling, critique-content, and critique-quality results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation 1 retain the same student-answer generation, teacher critique and refinement, and conditional likelihood training procedure. Prompt-only inference is also retained. Fresh sampling and inference-format explanations clarify the existing method; RGNR is a diagnostic, not a new training component.

E1.justification: v4 adds zero-shot HumanEval code generation, extending evaluation into a distinct domain, and adds AIME 2025. The original training datasets and mathematical/general-reasoning benchmarks remain. AIME24 already appeared in v3 Table 3; its later sampling study changes settings and results rather than introducing that benchmark.

E2.justification: The principal comparator families remain SFT, Distilled SFT, CFT, and SimpleRL-Zero. However, Section 4.1.2 changes the reported Distilled SFT target construction from teacher conditioning on prompt, student answer, and critique to conditioning on the prompt alone. v4 Table 3 also adds a teacher-matched CFT comparison for Qwen2.5-Math. Retained scores do not establish that Distilled SFT experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: v4 introduces Qwen2.5-Math-7B/Claude teacher configurations, greedy and temperature-0.6 Pass@k evaluation, and a roughly 10K-example experiment holding answers and targets fixed while varying critiques. The retained RL-context CGD results also receive a revised stated budget: v3 describes eight A100s for approximately five hours of fine-tuning, whereas v4 reports eight training GPU-hours plus approximately 40 generation GPU-hours. This does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: v4 adds specific/relevant versus irrelevant versus generic critique controls, a 20,000-critique quality analysis with length controls and judge calibration, pre-training RGNR diagnostics, lexical-overlap analysis, and AIME sampling/response-length analyses. Earlier critique-removal, correctness-mixture, training-stability, entropy, attention, and displayed counterfactual analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v3 already reports three-seed means, entropy significance tests, gradient standard deviations, and attention confidence intervals. v4 adds explicit mean±standard-deviation reporting for AIME and critique-content experiments, standard errors and a paired test for the retained gradient diagnostic, and effect-size/odds-ratio reporting for critique quality. It does not state that existing experiments received more runs.

E6.justification: Core Table 1 values and many earlier appendix results are unchanged, but substantial results are added. HumanEval reports 59.7% for the base model and 64.6% for CGD; the new LLaMA-Instruct AIME24 study reports greedy accuracy of 3.3% versus 16.7%. Qwen, AIME25, critique-content, quality, and RGNR results are also new. These are additional experiments, not improvements over v3 scores under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix G formalizes the RGNR receptivity criterion through a gradient-norm ratio and numerical interpretation thresholds. The training objective and Bayesian relation are retained. The new theoretical-motivation appendix supplies auxiliary-learning, curriculum, and representation explanations but explicitly offers no formal proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: v4 adds headline claims about code-domain transfer, critique specificity/relevance, and reasoning quality at low sampling budgets. It replaces v3's prominent 60x-compute and alternative-to-RL framing with an intermediate, complementary training paradigm. The conclusion also qualifies inference efficiency as absence of architectural overhead, while retaining the central CGD contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds auxiliary-supervision and representation-transfer explanations, interprets lexical overlap and AIME behavior as internalization, and distinguishes harmful training critiques from robustness after training. Limitations newly address creative/open-ended domains and informative-critique dependence. RL is interpreted as complementary exploration. Some robustness explanations become more definitive although the displayed counterfactual case remains the same.

D1.justification: v4 supplies exact critique/refinement generation prompts, discloses benchmark-overlap checking and removal, details new diagnostic procedures, and separates generation from training costs. Appendix J replaces v3's supplementary-code-archive statement with a public repository address. These improve documentation and access instructions; the PDFs do not establish that newly disclosed prompts or filtering were newly introduced, or verify repository availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the literature comparison, adding reasoning-trace distillation, on-policy distillation, critic/RL, and latent-reasoning approaches, including ORCA, GKD, SCOTT, and CODI. Much of the earlier tool-based and pedagogical-feedback survey is removed or condensed. The revised positioning emphasizes student-specific semantic feedback and training-only critique consumption.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, limitations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into cross-family, critique-signal, diagnostic, and stability sections. Existing diagnostic/data/code appendices move from C/D/E to D/F/J alongside new appendices. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column conference layout throughout. The old SFT/CFT/CGD comparison schematic is removed, while the existing CGD pipeline becomes Figure 1. The correctness-mixture plot moves into the main text, learning-rate plots are rearranged, and numerous experimental and summary tables are added. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The matched-target critique-content control strengthens v3's critique-removal evidence, while exact prompts, uncertainty reporting, broader evaluation, and fuller compute accounting improve transparency. Benefits are tempered by unresolved reporting problems: Distilled SFT's description changes despite retained scores; Table 3 reports a CFT/S1.1 average of 46.9 although its entries average 42.2; and Figure 3 incorrectly recasts a 114% gain as a drop. Strong internalization claims also exceed what lexical overlap alone establishes. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement.
